about: tools/workflows/recipes: rebuilt on the notice tables (devices, notices). Replaces tool:mark-my-notices-read in tools/tell-the-person, which read and wrote through the retired records door. A notice's read state is one column; the surface it was read on is not kept.

payload.label: Mark my notices read
payload.job: Mark one or more notices of the person read in the person's own database, so every device shows them as read.
payload.produces: The notices marked read, and whether any of them was unread before.

source.from: tools/tell-the-person read-data/told.mjs (markMyNoticesRead) and tool:mark-my-notices-read, read on the Workshop's origin/main 75fa3807fc, then rebuilt on notices.read_at
source.note: Marking is idempotent: a notice is written only while its read_at is null, so a repeated mark keeps the first time it was read.

database.description: The name of the person's own database, the one the workflow's tables live in (the store the account keeps its rows in).

steps.title: Make the notice tables if they are absent
steps.do: Run the statements of this step's sql, in order, through tool:run-sql-in-my-database with database = input.database. They only create what is missing, so a run where both tables exist changes nothing. Submit {rendered: true}.

sql.name: devices
sql.text: CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS devices (id text PRIMARY KEY, platform text NOT NULL CHECK (platform IN ('live', 'web-push', 'apns')), token text, app_build text, registered_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(), last_seen_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now())

sql.name: notices
sql.text: CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS notices (id bigint GENERATED ALWAYS AS IDENTITY PRIMARY KEY, device_id text REFERENCES devices (id), title text NOT NULL DEFAULT '', body text NOT NULL DEFAULT '', url text, made_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(), read_at timestamptz, acted_at timestamptz)

steps.title: Mark the notices read
steps.do: Check input.ids: a non-empty list of "told:<number>" strings, else refuse with "ids must be a list of told:<number> notice ids.". Make the notice numbers: the number after each "told:", as whole numbers, kept once each. Run the statement named found with params [notice numbers]: the rows it returns are the notices found; count them as n, and count the rows whose read_at is null as unread. Run the statement named mark with the same params; it writes only the notices still unread, so a repeated mark writes nothing. Answer {ids: the found notices as told:<number>, read: true, changed: true when unread is more than 0, said}, where said is "1 notice marked read." when n is 1, and "<n> notices marked read." otherwise.

sql.name: found
sql.text: SELECT id, read_at FROM notices WHERE id = ANY($1::bigint[])

sql.name: mark
sql.text: UPDATE notices SET read_at = now() WHERE id = ANY($1::bigint[]) AND read_at IS NULL
